# Practical coding

English · [Русский](../ru/themes/coding-practical.md) · [AI Interview Atlas](../../README.md) › [Themes](../README.md#themes)

Work-like coding: concurrency, rate limits, retries, evolving specifications, debugging and code review.

## <a id="track-both"></a>Both tracks

- <a id="code-refactoring"></a>**Refactor a small, poorly structured program with passing tests. Explain the first change and how you preserve observable behaviour.**

## <a id="track-engineering"></a>AI Engineering

- <a id="code-causal-attention"></a>**Implement scaled dot-product attention with a causal mask and tests that would expose attention to future tokens.**
  - Coding · Asked at: [Amazon](../companies/amazon.md) †, [Anthropic](../companies/anthropic.md) †, [Google and Google DeepMind](../companies/google.md) † · ✍ [Answer](../answers/engineering.md#code-causal-attention) · [Suggest a fix](https://github.com/eiler2005/ai-interview-atlas/issues/new?template=correction.yml&question=code-causal-attention&title=%5BCorrection%5D%20code-causal-attention)
  - Tests: Whether shapes, masking and numerical stability are correct in executable code.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Check batch, sequence and head dimensions before implementing score multiplication.
    - Use stable softmax after masking disallowed positions.
    - Test small hand-computable cases and ensure changing future inputs cannot change earlier outputs.
  - Read: [Attention Is All You Need](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762) (Vaswani et al., arXiv)
- <a id="code-grouped-attention"></a>**Implement multi-head attention, then modify the implementation so several query heads share each pair of key and value heads.**
  - Coding · Asked at: [Google and Google DeepMind](../companies/google.md) † · [Suggest a fix](https://github.com/eiler2005/ai-interview-atlas/issues/new?template=correction.yml&question=code-grouped-attention&title=%5BCorrection%5D%20code-grouped-attention)
  - Tests: Whether tensor layout and head grouping are implemented consistently.

  - Coding · [Suggest a fix](https://github.com/eiler2005/ai-interview-atlas/issues/new?template=correction.yml&question=code-cached-decode&title=%5BCorrection%5D%20code-cached-decode)

  - Tests: Whether probability mass, ties and invalid parameters are handled correctly.
- <a id="code-lru"></a>**Build a cache with constant-time lookup and recency updates, then add expiry without breaking eviction semantics.**
  - Coding · Asked at: [OpenAI](../companies/openai.md) † · [Suggest a fix](https://github.com/eiler2005/ai-interview-atlas/issues/new?template=correction.yml&question=code-lru&title=%5BCorrection%5D%20code-lru)
  - Tests: Whether data-structure invariants survive an evolving specification.
- <a id="code-token-bucket"></a>**Implement a token-bucket limiter and explain what must change when several workers enforce the same limit.**
  - Coding · Asked at: [Anthropic](../companies/anthropic.md) †, [OpenAI](../companies/openai.md) † · ✍ [Answer](../answers/engineering.md#code-token-bucket) · [Suggest a fix](https://github.com/eiler2005/ai-interview-atlas/issues/new?template=correction.yml&question=code-token-bucket&title=%5BCorrection%5D%20code-token-bucket)
  - Tests: Whether time accounting and concurrent updates preserve the quota.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Refill from elapsed monotonic time and cap tokens at capacity.
    - Make the check-and-consume operation atomic across competing calls.
    - Test bursts and time boundaries; state the shared-store or partitioning contract for distributed enforcement.
  - Read: [Scaling your API with rate limiters](https://stripe.com/blog/rate-limiters) (Stripe)
- <a id="code-async-batches"></a>**Write an asynchronous API batch processor with bounded concurrency, retry jitter and isolated per-item failures.**
  - Coding · Asked at: [Anthropic](../companies/anthropic.md) †, [Perplexity](../companies/perplexity.md) † · ✍ [Answer](../answers/engineering.md#code-async-batches) · [Suggest a fix](https://github.com/eiler2005/ai-interview-atlas/issues/new?template=correction.yml&question=code-async-batches&title=%5BCorrection%5D%20code-async-batches)
  - Tests: Whether cancellation, retries and results remain well-defined under partial failure.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Bound in-flight work and propagate cancellation and deadlines.
    - Retry only suitable failures with capped backoff and jitter; consider idempotency.
    - Return per-item outcomes and test timeouts, permanent failures and partial completion.
  - Read: [Designing robust and predictable APIs with idempotency](https://stripe.com/blog/idempotency) (Stripe) · [Site Reliability Engineering](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/) (Google)
